findings.text: Tracking record for one dynamic identifier holds an owning context marker and a synchronization generation. Stored generation is compared against incoming generation to decide whether cached entries remain valid, with equality or newer meaning reusable and older meaning flush required.

Per processor address space record keeps the currently loaded descriptor and a shared slot for last user descriptor or its encoded speculative variant, plus loaded and next identifier numbers, a flag requesting clearing of non loaded slots, an optional address masking mode, a mask of user identifiers pending flush, a software mirror of control register, and an array of tracking records sized by dynamic count.

Cross processor visible record holds a single laziness indicator distinguishing deferred reload retention from active use and from initial descriptor use, allowing remote invalidation paths to reason about membership without seeing private state.

Remote invalidation descriptor carries an optional target descriptor with an address interval and a generation to advance to, plus originating processor number and stride hint and indicators for freed tables and for mask maintenance. It is aligned to a small cache friendly boundary to allow efficient sharing.

Deferred unmap batch combines a processor set possibly caching affected frames with a flag recording that unmapping occurred even when no active processor was involved, supporting later collective invalidation.
System topology sizing table stores parallel shift and size arrays indexed by domain level from threading upward, providing base data for queries about package and die and core organization.

Domain levels progress from threading through core then module then tile then die then die group then package with a final count sentinel. Efficiency classes number performance first followed by efficiency then low power.
Number of dynamic identifiers managed per processor is six, fixing the size of tracking storage and the wrap point for allocation.
Full address range is represented by an end value with all bits set. Invalid generation is represented by zero, never used as a valid synchronization point.

Transient marker used for loaded descriptor during the brief interrupts disabled switch window has numeric value one, distinct from any valid descriptor pointer and recognizable by non maskable checks.
Alignment required for remote invalidation descriptors is the smaller of processor cache line size and sixty four, keeping records compact yet avoiding false sharing.

Broadcast invalidation control bits assign successive low positions to virtual address selection and process context selection and address space selection and global inclusion and final level only and nested inclusion. Mode value zero means all non globals. Stride distinguishes normal pages from large pages.
Each public header provides a unique inclusion guard macro that prevents double inclusion when the same translation unit references the header repeatedly.

Selection result pairs an identifier with a flush indicator that is required whenever hardware context support is missing or no stored identity matches or stored generation predates incoming generation, and is avoided only on generation current reuse or on hardware coherent global reuse without local tracking.

After handling a pending cross slot invalidation request under isolation, all non loaded stored identities are reset to force later flush while the loaded slot is untouched and the request flag is cleared. Invocation without isolation is unexpected and warned.

Control register loading for a new descriptor records user side flush need when required then writes either a flushing or a non flushing combined value. Non flushing construction assumes process context support and sets a no flush control bit. User side recording is skipped entirely when isolation is disabled at build or at runtime or when context support is absent, otherwise it marks the kernel view of the identifier in a per processor mask.

Context switch mitigation tracks an encoded combination of incoming descriptor address with predictor and cache flush request bits derived from thread flags. Predictor barrier is issued on descriptor or request change under conditional or always policies. Cache flush of outgoing request is immediate, while incoming cache request on a threaded sibling arranges deferred termination signaling and clears the request flag.

Performance counter access control enables user cycle reading only when globally forced or when not globally denied and the descriptor allows it, clearing stale counter state before enabling to avoid disclosure, otherwise disabling access. An alternate build provides an empty operation with no register effect.

Mask maintenance is rate limited to at most once per second per descriptor using a monotonic clock and a stored deadline that is advanced on success. Flush descriptor initialization collapses oversized intervals to full range based on a page count ceiling, then records interval and target and stride and table free flag and generation and originator while clearing the trim request.

Single address invalidation issues a privileged operation for the given virtual address. Broadcast address flush without synchronization targets page granularity with global inclusion for a small count. Global full flush toggles the global enable control off then on to discard all global entries.

One lazy entry variant leaves initial descriptor use unchanged and otherwise marks shared state lazy without touching loaded state. Additional build variants and self presence markers exist for portability, and control shadow is captured once from hardware for later protected updates.

Range flush selects large page sizing for huge mappings and normal sizing otherwise. Single page flush covers exactly one page without table free indication. Deferral is chosen when any remote processor shares the descriptor mask. Pending batch update advances generation and merges masks and records unmapping and notifies secondary agents for full range.

Permission change evaluation ignores software scratch bits and optionally ignores access. Clearing of dirty or present or accessed requires flush, as does any change to writability or user access or caching or large mapping or global or key rights or execute control. Absent old entries need no flush, differing frames always need flush, otherwise flag evaluation applies with access ignored for normal pages but considered for large mappings. Alternate builds provide equivalent availability markers.

Domain size query reads the system table directly, while shift query returns zero for threading and otherwise reads the predecessor entry. Early mapping and node identification and mask setup each offer a trivial fallback reporting zero or doing nothing alongside a table backed version for multi node builds.

Public node and topology queries are thin aliases over internal per processor and per bus tables, exposing processor to node conversion and bus to node conversion and node distance plus logical and physical identifiers for package and die and core and protection and vendor node values.

Headers export control register bit set and clear helpers in both interrupt protected and caller protected forms, plus single address and broadcast invalidation operations and range and page flush operations with batch deferral and pending update helpers.

Software mirror of control register and hardware register itself are modified only with interrupts disabled. Caller protected variants require disabled interrupts on entry, while public variants save interrupt state around the protected update and restore it after.

Processor address space use moves among active membership with immediate reload, lazy membership with deferred reload, and initial descriptor without membership. Transition to lazy applies only outside initial use and only sets the shared flag, leaving loaded state for later reload and allowing remote logic to observe laziness.

Dynamic identifier lifecycle starts unmatched then becomes associated with a stored identity and generation, remains reusable while generation stays current, requires flush when generation advances or when cross slot invalidation is pending, and is eventually recycled by wrapping allocation after all slots are consumed, with global hardware coherent values bypassing local lifecycle entirely.

Invalidation descriptors distinguish full single target advancement and bounded single target advancement covering changes between successive generations and global advancement of all targets. Initialization chooses between bounded and full single target forms based on estimated page count, while global form uses null target and zero generation.

Callable flush entry points include range based and single page based invalidation with automatic sizing, batch deferral decision based on remote membership, batch pending accumulation with generation advance and mask merge, and low level single address and broadcast and global operations.

Callable topology entry points include domain size and shift queries indexed by level, early processor to node mapping, node identification, mask setup, and alias based conversions for processor and bus to node with distance and per processor identifier reads.

Predictor and cache side channel hazards are addressed by barrier issuance on cross descriptor switches with relevant requests and by immediate cache flush for outgoing requests. Incoming cache requests scheduled on a threaded sibling are unsafe due to shared cache and instead trigger deferred termination signaling, with request state cleared to avoid repeated action.

Correctness hazards include use of stale identifiers after generation advance, missed cross slot invalidation when isolation expectations are violated, disclosure via stale performance state when enabling user counters, reliance on serializing register writes for ordering with mask updates, paravirtual flushes that bypass generation accounting, special handling of slot zero during early initialization, and unexpected faults if flush decisions ignore required permission changes.
